source.text: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן יָ֗מָּה וְכָל־מַלְכֵ֤י הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַיָּ֔ם אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֵ֧י הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן מִפְּנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־עָבְרָ֑ם וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבָ֗ם וְלֹא־הָ֨יָה בָ֥ם עוֹד֙ ר֔וּחַ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard all [the] kings of the Amorites who [were] beyond the Jordan westward, and all [the] kings of the Canaanites who [were] by the sea, how dried up YHWH [the] waters of the Jordan before [the] sons of Israel until they crossed, and melted their heart, and there was not in them still spirit before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And it happened, when all the kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan to the west, and all the kings of the Canaanites who [were] by the sea, heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel until they had crossed over, that their heart melted, and there was no longer spirit in them because of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: All the kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan and all the kings of the Canaanites along the sea heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made the waters of the Jordan dry up ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} until they had crossed. When they heard it, their hearts melted, and no spirit was left in them to face the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the coast heard what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done. He had dried up the Jordan River so that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} could cross. When the kings heard this, they lost all their courage. They were too afraid of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to stand up to them.

sw.L: Ikawa wafalme wote wa Waamori waliokuwa ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa magharibi, na wafalme wote wa Wakanaani waliokuwa karibu na bahari, waliposikia jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameyakausha maji ya Yordani mbele ya wana wa Israeli mpaka walipokwisha kuvuka, moyo wao ukayeyuka, wala haikuwamo tena roho ndani yao kwa sababu ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Wafalme wote wa Waamori upande wa magharibi wa Yordani, na wafalme wote wa Wakanaani kando ya bahari, walisikia jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoyakausha maji ya Yordani mbele ya Waisraeli mpaka walipomaliza kuvuka. Waliposikia hayo, mioyo yao iliyeyuka, wala hawakubaki na ujasiri wa kuwakabili Waisraeli.
sw.R: Wafalme wa Waamori upande wa magharibi wa Mto Yordani, na wafalme wa Wakanaani kando ya pwani, walisikia yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amefanya. Alikuwa ameukausha Mto Yordani ili Waisraeli waweze kuvuka. Wafalme hao waliposikia habari hiyo, walikata tamaa kabisa. Waliwaogopa Waisraeli mno, hata hawakuthubutu kupigana nao.

decisions.choice: until they crossed
decisions.reason: The written form of the Hebrew consonants reads "until we crossed", as if the narrator counted himself among those who crossed (compare "to give to us" in verse 6). The form the scribes marked to be read aloud, which this text follows, has "they crossed". The event is the same either way.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan to the west; by the sea: the hill country west of the river and the coast of the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: Elsewhere "across the Jordan" often means the east side, but "westward" makes it plain that these kings rule in Canaan itself, the land Israel has just entered. "The sea" is the Great Sea to the west (1:4). Together the two groups stand for all the kings of the land.

decisions.choice: their heart melted, and there was no longer spirit in them: they lost all courage
decisions.reason: A melting heart is a picture of fear that takes away the will to fight (2:11; 7:5). "Spirit" here is breath or courage, not the Spirit of God. Rahab had already said the same of the people of Jericho (2:9-11).

decisions.choice: too afraid of the Israelites to stand up to them
decisions.reason: "No spirit before the Israelites" means they had no courage to face them. Readable says so plainly.

source.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ עֲשֵׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וְשׁ֛וּב מֹ֥ל אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: At the time the that said YHWH to Joshua, make for yourself knives of flints and again circumcise [the] sons of Israel a second [time].

en.L: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Make for yourself knives of flint, and again circumcise the sons of Israel a second time."
en.B: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Make knives of flint and once more circumcise the sons of Israel, a second time."
en.R: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Joshua, "Make knives out of flint. Then circumcise the men and boys of Israel again, as was done before."

sw.L: Wakati huo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Yoshua, "Jifanyie visu vya mawe magumu, ukawatahiri tena wana wa Israeli mara ya pili."
sw.B: Wakati huo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Tengeneza visu vya mawe magumu, uwatahiri tena wanaume wa Israeli, mara ya pili."
sw.R: Wakati huo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Tengeneza visu kwa mawe magumu. Kisha uwatahiri tena wanaume na wavulana wa Israeli, kama ilivyofanyika zamani."

decisions.choice: knives of flint: blades of sharpened stone
decisions.reason: Flint could be chipped to a very sharp edge, and stone blades were used for circumcision long after metal tools were common (Exodus 4:25). Using them may also have kept an old, set way of doing a holy act.

decisions.choice: again ... a second time: the nation is circumcised once more, not the same men twice
decisions.reason: Verses 4-7 explain the words. The men who left Egypt had been circumcised, but their sons born in the wilderness had not. Israel as a people now receives the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:10-14) a second time; no one is circumcised twice.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel (no inclusive wording); Readable: the men and boys of Israel
decisions.reason: Only males were circumcised, so "sons" here means just what it says, and the inclusive wording used elsewhere for this phrase would be wrong. The same holds in verse 3.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" (L); "wanaume wa Israeli" (B); "wanaume na wavulana wa Israeli" (R)
decisions.reason: Here only males are meant, since the subject is circumcision, so Balanced does not use the usual "Waisraeli" (all Israelites). Literal keeps "wana wa Israeli", in which "wana" can mean sons. Verses 3 to 8 follow the same rule.

decisions.choice: "visu vya mawe magumu"
decisions.reason: "Gumegume" is the precise word for flint but is little known; "mawe magumu" (hard stones) says what the knives were made of in words every reader knows.

source.text: וַיַּעַשׂ־ל֥וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וַיָּ֨מָל֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־גִּבְעַ֖ת הָעֲרָלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And made for himself Joshua knives of flints and circumcised [the] sons of Israel at [the] hill of the foreskins.

en.L: And Joshua made for himself knives of flint, and he circumcised the sons of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.
en.B: So Joshua made knives of flint, and at the Hill of Foreskins he circumcised the sons of Israel.
en.R: So Joshua made knives out of flint. He circumcised the men and boys of Israel at a place called Foreskin Hill.

sw.L: Yoshua akajifanyia visu vya mawe magumu, akawatahiri wana wa Israeli kwenye Kilima cha Magovi.
sw.B: Basi Yoshua alitengeneza visu vya mawe magumu, akawatahiri wanaume wa Israeli kwenye Kilima cha Magovi.
sw.R: Basi Yoshua alitengeneza visu kwa mawe magumu. Akawatahiri wanaume na wavulana wa Israeli mahali palipoitwa Kilima cha Magovi.

decisions.choice: the Hill of the Foreskins: a place near Gilgal named from what was done there
decisions.reason: The phrase may be a place name (Gibeath-haaraloth) or a description of the spot where the foreskins were buried or left. Either way it marks the place by the event, as Gilgal is marked in verse 9.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel; Readable: the men and boys of Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: only males are meant.

source.text: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַיֹּצֵא֩ מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם הַזְּכָרִ֜ים כֹּ֣ל׀אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה מֵ֤תוּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] the reason that circumcised Joshua: all the people the coming out from Egypt, the males, all [the] men of the war, died in the wilderness on the way when they came out from Egypt.

en.L: And this [is] the reason why Joshua circumcised [them]: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt.
en.B: This is why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, every man of fighting age, had died in the wilderness on the way after they left Egypt.
en.R: This is why Joshua did it. All the men who were old enough to be soldiers when they left Egypt had died in the desert during the journey.

sw.L: Na hii [ndiyo] sababu Yoshua aliwatahiri: watu wote waliotoka Misri, wanaume, watu wote wa vita, walikuwa wamekufa nyikani njiani, baada ya kutoka Misri.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo sababu Yoshua aliwatahiri: watu wote waliotoka Misri, wanaume wote, kila mwanamume aliyefikia umri wa vita, walikuwa wamekufa nyikani njiani baada ya kutoka Misri.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo sababu Yoshua alifanya hivyo. Wanaume wote waliokuwa na umri wa kuwa askari walipotoka Misri walikuwa wamekufa jangwani wakati wa safari.

decisions.choice: the men of war: the males old enough for military service
decisions.reason: The census counted every male twenty years old and over who could go out to war (Numbers 1:3). That generation was condemned to die in the wilderness (Numbers 14:29-35; 26:64-65).

decisions.choice: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males: the words narrow the group step by step
decisions.reason: "All the people" is at once limited to "the males" and then to "all the men of war". The verse is about those who could have been circumcised and fought, not every person who left Egypt.

decisions.choice: circumcised [them]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the object to be understood from verse 3.

source.text: כִּֽי־מֻלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כָּל־הָעָ֖ם הַיֹּֽצְאִ֑ים וְכָל־הָ֠עָם הַיִּלֹּדִ֨ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֥ם מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם לֹא־מָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For circumcised were all the people the coming out, but all the people the born in the wilderness on the way when they came out from Egypt not they circumcised.

en.L: For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people who were born in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt, they had not circumcised.
en.B: All the people who came out had been circumcised, but none of the people born in the wilderness on the journey after leaving Egypt had been circumcised.
en.R: All the men who came out of Egypt had been circumcised. But the boys born in the desert during the journey had not been circumcised.

sw.L: Kwa maana watu wote waliotoka walikuwa wametahiriwa, lakini watu wote waliozaliwa nyikani njiani, baada ya kutoka Misri, hawakuwatahiri.
sw.B: Watu wote waliotoka Misri walikuwa wametahiriwa, lakini hakuna hata mmoja wa watu waliozaliwa nyikani wakati wa safari baada ya kutoka Misri aliyekuwa ametahiriwa.
sw.R: Wanaume wote waliotoka Misri walikuwa wametahiriwa. Lakini wavulana waliozaliwa jangwani wakati wa safari hawakuwa wametahiriwa.

decisions.choice: they had not circumcised: no one had circumcised them
decisions.reason: The verb is active with no named subject, a common Hebrew way of saying that something was not done. The text gives no reason why circumcision stopped in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the men ... the boys
decisions.reason: "All the people" here means the males, as verse 4 has just said. Readable names them as men and boys so a reader does not think of women being circumcised.

source.text: כִּ֣י׀אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה הָלְכ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ עַד־תֹּ֨ם כָּל־הַגּ֜וֹי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הַיֹּצְאִ֣ים מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֞י הַרְאוֹתָ֣ם אֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה לַֽאֲבוֹתָם֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔נוּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For forty years walked [the] sons of Israel in the wilderness until was finished all the nation, [the] men of the war the coming out from Egypt, who not listened to [the] voice of YHWH, to whom swore YHWH to them not to let them see the land that swore YHWH to their fathers to give to us, a land flowing of milk and honey.

en.L: For forty years the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel walked in the wilderness, until all the nation was finished, the men of war who came out of Egypt, who had not listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not let them see the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to their fathers to give to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
en.B: For forty years the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} traveled in the wilderness, until that whole nation, the men of war who had come out of Egypt, had perished, because they had not listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} swore to them that they would not see the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised their fathers on oath to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} traveled in the desert for forty years. In that time all the men who had left Egypt old enough to fight died, because they had not obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had sworn that they would never see the land. It was the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised with an oath to their ancestors to give to us, a rich land flowing with milk and honey.

sw.L: Kwa maana wana wa Israeli walitembea nyikani miaka arobaini, mpaka taifa lote lilipokwisha, watu wa vita waliotoka Misri, ambao hawakuisikiliza sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia kwamba hatawaacha waione nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia baba zao kwamba atatupa, nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali.
sw.B: Kwa maana Waisraeli walisafiri nyikani miaka arobaini, mpaka taifa lile lote, watu wa vita waliotoka Misri, lilipokwisha kufa, kwa sababu hawakuisikiliza sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia kwamba hawataiona nchi aliyowaahidi baba zao kwa kiapo kwamba atatupa, nchi itiririkayo maziwa na asali.
sw.R: Waisraeli walisafiri jangwani kwa miaka arobaini. Katika muda huo wanaume wote waliotoka Misri wakiwa na umri wa kupigana walikufa, kwa sababu hawakumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameapa kwamba hawataiona kamwe nchi ile. Ilikuwa nchi aliyowaahidi babu zao kwa kiapo kwamba atatupa, nchi tajiri itiririkayo maziwa na asali.

decisions.choice: forty years ... until they were finished: the sentence of Numbers 14
decisions.reason: After the people refused to enter the land, the LORD swore that the adults of that generation would wander forty years and die in the wilderness, and that their children would enter instead (Numbers 14:21-35; Deuteronomy 1:34-39; 2:14-16).

decisions.choice: did not listen to the voice of the LORD: did not obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say (Exodus 19:5). The fault in view is the refusal to go up into the land (Numbers 14:22).

decisions.choice: to give to us: the narrator counts himself among Israel
decisions.reason: The oath was made to the fathers, but the gift is to "us", the people who now live in the land. The speaker stands with the generation that entered (compare the written form "we crossed" in verse 1).

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich, fertile land
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Canaan from Exodus 3:8 on. Milk speaks of good pasture for flocks, and honey of sweetness and plenty (honey from bees or a syrup from dates or figs).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forefathers of the nation, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob among them. Readable uses the plainer word.

source.text: וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ הֵקִ֣ים תַּחְתָּ֔ם אֹתָ֖ם מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּי־עֲרֵלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כִּ֛י לֹא־מָ֥לוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And their sons he raised up in their place; them circumcised Joshua, for uncircumcised they were, for not they had circumcised them on the way.

en.L: And their sons {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised up in their place; them Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them on the way.
en.B: It was their sons, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised up in their place, that Joshua circumcised. They were uncircumcised, because no one had circumcised them on the way.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} raised up their sons to take their place. These were the ones Joshua circumcised. They had not been circumcised during the journey.

sw.L: Na wana wao, aliowainua mahali pao, hao ndio Yoshua aliowatahiri, kwa maana walikuwa hawajatahiriwa, kwa sababu hawakuwa wamewatahiri njiani.
sw.B: Wana wao, ambao alikuwa amewainua mahali pao, ndio Yoshua aliowatahiri. Walikuwa hawajatahiriwa, kwa sababu hakuna aliyewatahiri njiani.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwainua wana wao wachukue nafasi yao. Hao ndio Yoshua aliowatahiri. Walikuwa hawajatahiriwa wakati wa safari.

decisions.choice: he raised up: the LORD, the subject of verse 6
decisions.reason: The one who swore that the fathers would not see the land is the one who raised up their sons in their place, as he had said he would (Numbers 14:31).

decisions.choice: uncircumcised: without the sign of the covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision marked a male as belonging to God's covenant people (Genesis 17:10-14). Before Israel keeps the Passover (verse 10), every male must bear it (Exodus 12:48).

decisions.choice: The LORD raised up
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew carries over from verse 6.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁר־תַּ֥מּוּ כָל־הַגּ֖וֹי לְהִמּ֑וֹל וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה עַ֥ד חֲיוֹתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had finished all the nation to be circumcised, and they remained in their place in the camp until they lived.

en.L: And it happened, when all the nation had finished being circumcised, that they stayed in their places in the camp until they recovered.
en.B: When the circumcising of the whole nation was finished, they stayed where they were in the camp until they had healed.
en.R: After all the men were circumcised, they stayed in the camp until they were well again.

sw.L: Ikawa taifa lote lilipomaliza kutahiriwa, wakakaa mahali pao kambini mpaka walipopona.
sw.B: Kutahiriwa kwa taifa lote kulipokwisha, walikaa mahali pao kambini mpaka walipopona.
sw.R: Baada ya wanaume wote kutahiriwa, walikaa kambini mpaka walipopona.

decisions.choice: they lived: they recovered, were healed
decisions.reason: The verb "live" can mean to come back to health (2 Kings 1:2; 8:8). The men were unable to fight for some days (compare Genesis 34:25), yet Israel was camped in enemy country without being attacked, because of the fear in verse 1.

decisions.choice: all the men
decisions.reason: "All the nation" here means all who needed to be circumcised (verses 4-7). Readable says so.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֗וֹם גַּלּ֛וֹתִי אֶת־חֶרְפַּ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ גִּלְגָּ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to Joshua, the day I have rolled away [the] reproach of Egypt from on you; and called [one] [the] name of the place the that Gilgal until the day the this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." And [one] called the name of that place Gilgal, until this day.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt." So that place is called Gilgal to this day.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away from you the shame of Egypt." That is why the place is still called Gilgal. The name sounds like the word meaning to roll away.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Yoshua, "Leo nimeivingirisha mbali nanyi aibu ya Misri." Na jina la mahali pale likaitwa Gilgali, hadi siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Leo nimeivingirisha mbali nanyi aibu ya Misri." Kwa hiyo mahali pale panaitwa Gilgali hadi leo.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Leo nimeiondoa kwenu aibu ya Misri, kama mtu anavyovingirisha jiwe mbali." Ndiyo sababu mahali pale bado panaitwa Gilgali. Jina hilo linasikika kama neno la Kiebrania lenye maana ya kuvingirisha.

decisions.choice: Gilgal: the name is tied by its sound to the verb galal, "roll"
alternatives: Gilgal named only from a circle of stones
decisions.reason: The LORD says "I have rolled away" (gallothi), and the place is called Gilgal. The play on sounds explains what the name means to Israel from now on. The name itself may first have meant "circle", perhaps after the circle of stones set up there (4:19-20); the text gives it a new sense from this day.

decisions.choice: the reproach of Egypt: the shame that clung to Israel from Egypt, now removed
alternatives: the disgrace of slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: The text does not say exactly what this shame was. It may be the disgrace of having been slaves in Egypt; or the Egyptians' taunt that the LORD had brought Israel out only to let them die in the wilderness (Exodus 32:12; Numbers 14:13-16; Deuteronomy 9:28), a taunt answered now that Israel is in the land; or the state of being uncircumcised, which Scripture can count as a disgrace (Genesis 34:14). Whatever its form, it ends with this day at Gilgal.

decisions.choice: called ... until this day: the name was still in use when the account was written
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject and means that the place came to be called so. "Until this day" looks from the writer's own time back to the event (4:9).

decisions.choice: The name sounds like the word meaning to roll away.
decisions.reason: Without a note, a reader of Readable cannot see why "rolled away" explains the name. The added sentence states the link the Hebrew makes by sound.

decisions.choice: disgrace (Balanced); shame (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means scorn or insult heaped on someone. "Reproach" stays at Literal; the other levels use commoner words.

decisions.choice: "kama mtu anavyovingirisha jiwe mbali" added at Readable
decisions.reason: "Kuvingirisha aibu" is not a Swahili figure, so Readable says how the word "roll" is meant, so that the play on the name Gilgal that follows can be understood.

source.text: וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֡סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בָּעֶ֖רֶב בְּעַֽרְב֥וֹת יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And camped [the] sons of Israel at Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on four-teen day of the month in the evening, on [the] plains of Jericho.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel camped at Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
en.B: While the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were camped at Gilgal, they kept the Passover in the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, on the plains of Jericho.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} camped at Gilgal on the plains near Jericho. There, on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, they celebrated the Passover.

sw.L: Wana wa Israeli wakapiga kambi huko Gilgali, wakaifanya Pasaka siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi, jioni, katika nchi tambarare za Yeriko.
sw.B: Waisraeli walipokuwa wamepiga kambi huko Gilgali, waliiadhimisha Pasaka jioni ya siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi, katika nchi tambarare za Yeriko.
sw.R: Waisraeli walipiga kambi huko Gilgali katika nchi tambarare karibu na Yeriko. Huko, jioni ya siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa kwanza, waliiadhimisha Pasaka.

decisions.choice: the Passover on the fourteenth day, in the evening: kept on the day the law sets
decisions.reason: The law sets the Passover at evening on the fourteenth day of the first month (Exodus 12:6; Leviticus 23:5; Numbers 9:1-5). Israel crossed the Jordan on the tenth day (4:19), so the date follows on from that. The last Passover the text records before this was kept at Sinai (Numbers 9:5).

decisions.choice: they kept the Passover: possible now that the males are circumcised
decisions.reason: No uncircumcised male could eat the Passover (Exodus 12:43-49). The circumcision of verses 2-8 makes the people fit to keep it, and the first feast in the land recalls the first one in Egypt.

decisions.choice: the plains of Jericho: the flat land of the Jordan valley around Jericho
decisions.reason: The word names the low, open floor of the Jordan valley. Israel had camped on the other side, on the plains of Moab (Numbers 22:1); now they are across, near the city they will face first.

decisions.choice: the first month
decisions.reason: "The month" is the first month of the year, the month of the exodus (4:19; Exodus 12:2). Readable says so.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אכְל֜וּ מֵעֲב֥וּר הָאָ֛רֶץ מִמָּֽחֳרַ֥ת הַפֶּ֖סַח מַצּ֣וֹת וְקָל֑וּי בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they ate from [the] produce of the land on [the] day after the Passover, unleavened cakes and roasted [grain], on [the] very day the this.

en.L: And they ate from the produce of the land on the day after the Passover, unleavened bread and roasted [grain], on this very day.
en.B: On the day after the Passover, that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain.
en.R: That very day, the day after the Passover, they ate some of the food grown in the land. They ate bread made without yeast, and roasted grain.

sw.L: Wakala katika mazao ya nchi siku iliyofuata Pasaka, mikate isiyotiwa chachu na [nafaka] iliyokaangwa, siku hiyo hiyo.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata Pasaka, siku hiyo hiyo, walikula baadhi ya mazao ya nchi: mikate isiyotiwa chachu na nafaka iliyokaangwa.
sw.R: Siku hiyo hiyo, siku iliyofuata Pasaka, walikula baadhi ya chakula kilichootea katika nchi hiyo. Walikula mikate isiyotiwa chachu na nafaka iliyokaangwa.

decisions.choice: the produce of the land: grain grown in Canaan
decisions.reason: The word is rare, found only here and in verse 12, and means what the land yields. It was the time of the barley harvest (3:15), so grain was ready in the fields.

decisions.choice: the day after the Passover: the fifteenth day, the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: The same phrase marks the day Israel set out from Egypt (Numbers 33:3). The day after the Passover begins the seven days of unleavened bread (Leviticus 23:5-6), so the first food of the new land is eaten on the anniversary of the exodus.

decisions.choice: unleavened bread and roasted grain: quick food from new grain
decisions.reason: Unleavened bread is flat bread made without yeast, as the feast required (Exodus 12:15). Roasted grain was fresh ears parched over a fire and eaten at once (Leviticus 23:14; Ruth 2:14).

decisions.choice: roasted [grain]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "roasted"; the word is regularly used of grain.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֨ת הַמָּ֜ן מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת בְּאָכְלָם֙ מֵעֲב֣וּר הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מָ֑ן וַיֹּאכְל֗וּ מִתְּבוּאַת֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽיא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And ceased the manna on [the] next day when they ate from [the] produce of the land, and there was not again for [the] sons of Israel manna; and they ate from [the] yield of [the] land of Canaan in the year the that.

en.L: And the manna ceased on the next day, when they ate from the produce of the land, and there was no longer manna for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and they ate from the yield of the land of Canaan in that year.
en.B: The manna stopped on the day after they ate from the produce of the land. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had no more manna; that year they ate from the crops of the land of Canaan.
en.R: The manna stopped coming the day after they ate this food. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} never had manna again. That year they ate the food that grew in the land of Canaan.

sw.L: Mana ikakoma siku iliyofuata, walipokula katika mazao ya nchi, wala hapakuwa tena na mana kwa wana wa Israeli; nao wakala katika mavuno ya nchi ya Kanaani mwaka ule.
sw.B: Mana ilikoma siku iliyofuata baada ya kula mazao ya nchi. Waisraeli hawakuwa na mana tena; mwaka ule walikula mavuno ya nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.R: Mana iliacha kushuka siku iliyofuata baada ya kula chakula hicho. Waisraeli hawakupata mana tena. Mwaka ule walikula chakula kilichootea katika nchi ya Kanaani.

decisions.choice: the manna ceased: God's wilderness provision ends when the land's food begins
decisions.reason: The manna was given for forty years "until they came to a land where people lived" (Exodus 16:35). Its end shows that Israel's wandering is over and that God now feeds them from the land he promised.

decisions.choice: on the next day, when they ate: the day after they first ate the land's produce
alternatives: on the day after the Passover, the day they first ate
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "the day after the Passover", repeating verse 11, so that the manna stopped the same day they first ate the land's food. Read with "when they ate", the more natural sense is that it stopped the following day. Either way there was no day without food.

decisions.choice: crops
decisions.reason: This is a different word from "produce" in the first half of the verse, meaning the harvest or yield of the land. Balanced marks the change with a different word.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בִּירִיחוֹ֒ וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדּ֔וֹ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלוּפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ הֲלָ֥נוּ אַתָּ֖ה אִם־לְצָרֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when was Joshua by Jericho, and he lifted his eyes and saw, and look, a man standing before him, and his sword drawn in his hand; and went Joshua to him and said to him, [are] for us you, or for our adversaries?

en.L: And it happened, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted his eyes and looked, and look, a man was standing in front of him, and his sword [was] drawn in his hand. And Joshua went to him and said to him, "[Are] you for us, or for our enemies?"
en.B: Once, when Joshua was close to Jericho, he looked up, and there in front of him stood a man with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went over to him and asked, "Are you on our side, or on the side of our enemies?"
en.R: One day Joshua was near the city of Jericho. When he looked up, he saw a man standing there facing him. The man was holding a sword, ready to use it. Joshua went to him and asked, "Are you on our side, or on our enemies' side?"

sw.L: Ikawa Yoshua alipokuwa karibu na Yeriko, akainua macho yake akatazama, na tazama, mtu mmoja alikuwa amesimama mbele yake, na upanga wake [ukiwa] umefutwa mkononi mwake. Yoshua akamwendea, akamwambia, "[Je,] wewe [u] upande wetu, au upande wa adui zetu?"
sw.B: Wakati mmoja Yoshua alipokuwa karibu na Yeriko, aliinua macho, na hapo mbele yake alisimama mtu aliyeshika upanga uliofutwa mkononi mwake. Yoshua alimwendea, akamwuliza, "Je, wewe uko upande wetu au upande wa adui zetu?"
sw.R: Siku moja Yoshua alikuwa karibu na mji wa Yeriko. Alipoinua macho, aliona mtu amesimama mbele yake. Mtu huyo alikuwa ameshika upanga, tayari kuutumia. Yoshua alimwendea, akamwuliza, "Je, uko upande wetu, au upande wa adui zetu?"

decisions.choice: by Jericho: near the city, within sight of it
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "in" or "at", but Jericho's gates were shut against Israel (6:1). Joshua is close to the city, perhaps looking it over.

decisions.choice: a man: the figure appears as a man, and Joshua takes him for one
decisions.reason: Heavenly visitors are often first seen simply as men (Genesis 18:2; 32:25; Judges 13:6-11). Only his answer in verse 14 shows who he is.

decisions.choice: his sword drawn in his hand: ready to act as a warrior
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of the angel of the LORD who blocks Balaam's road (Numbers 22:23, 31) and of the angel sent against Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21:16). A drawn sword means he has come to fight, which is why Joshua asks whose side he is on.

decisions.choice: and look
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws the reader to look at what Joshua sees. Literal keeps it with a plain word; the other levels show the surprise by the order of the sentence.

decisions.choice: holding a sword, ready to use it
decisions.reason: "Drawn" means taken out of its sheath. Readable says what that shows.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לֹ֗א כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י שַׂר־צְבָֽא־יְהוָ֖ה עַתָּ֣ה בָ֑אתִי וַיִּפֹּל֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ אֶל־פָּנָ֥יו אַ֨רְצָה֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֲדֹנִ֖י מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, no, but I [am the] commander of [the] army of YHWH; now I have come. And fell Joshua to his face to [the] ground, and bowed down, and said to him, what [is] my lord speaking to his slave?

en.L: And he said, "No, but I [am the] commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; now I have come." And Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and he said to him, "What [is] my lord saying to his slave?"
en.B: "Neither," he answered. "I am the commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and now I have come." Then Joshua threw himself down with his face to the ground and bowed low. He said to him, "What does my lord wish to say to his servant?"
en.R: "No," he said. "I am the commander of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s army. I have come now." Then Joshua bowed down low with his face to the ground. He said, "My lord, I am your servant. What do you want to tell me?"

sw.L: Akasema, "Hapana, bali mimi [ni] mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; sasa nimekuja." Yoshua akaanguka kifudifudi hadi chini, akasujudu, akamwambia, "Bwana wangu anamwambia nini mtumwa wake?"
sw.B: Akajibu, "Hapana. Mimi ni mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na sasa nimekuja." Ndipo Yoshua alijitupa chini kifudifudi, akasujudu. Akamwambia, "Bwana wangu anataka kumwambia nini mtumishi wake?"
sw.R: Akasema, "Hapana. Mimi ni mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nimekuja sasa." Ndipo Yoshua aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi. Akasema, "Bwana wangu, mimi ni mtumishi wako. Unataka kuniambia nini?"

decisions.choice: No
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "no". Some manuscripts and the old Greek and Syriac translations read a word that sounds the same and means "to him" ("and he said to him"). The text here follows "no": he is not on either side as Joshua means it, because he comes for the LORD. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: the commander of the army of the LORD: a heavenly leader sent by the LORD; whether he is the LORD himself is not said
alternatives: the LORD himself appearing as a man
a chief angel who leads the LORD's heavenly army
decisions.reason: "The army of the LORD" is most likely the host of heaven, the angels who serve him (1 Kings 22:19; Psalm 103:20-21), though Israel's own tribes are once called "the armies of the LORD" (Exodus 12:41). The figure accepts Joshua's bowing and calls the ground holy (verse 15), as God does at the burning bush, where the angel of the LORD and God himself both speak (Exodus 3:2-6). In 6:2 the LORD speaks to Joshua, so the commander may be the LORD appearing in a man's form, as the angel of the LORD sometimes speaks as God (Genesis 16:7-13; 22:11-16; Numbers 22:22-35). But the text calls him only a man and a commander, Joshua addresses him as a man would a superior, and he may be an angel who comes with the LORD's authority. The passage leaves the question open.

decisions.choice: now I have come: his arrival is itself the message; what he came to say may follow in 6:2-5
alternatives: now I have come [to do something not stated]
decisions.reason: The words stand without a stated purpose. They may mean simply that he has now arrived to fight for Israel. The account may also break off here and continue in 6:2, where the LORD gives Joshua the plan for taking Jericho, with 6:1 as an aside.

decisions.choice: fell on his face and bowed down ... my lord ... his servant: the honor paid to a superior
decisions.reason: To fall face down and call oneself someone's servant is how a person shows deep respect, to a king or a heavenly visitor as well as to God (Genesis 18:2-3; 1 Samuel 25:23-24). The word for "my lord" here is the form used for a human master or a messenger, not the title reserved for God, so Joshua's words do not by themselves settle who the commander is.

decisions.choice: my lord (small l); slave at Literal, servant at Balanced and Readable; no capitalized pronouns for the commander
decisions.reason: Joshua uses the ordinary polite form of address, so "lord" is not capitalized, and because the text does not say plainly that the commander is God, the pronouns for him are not treated as pronouns for God (compare the angel of the LORD in Numbers 22). "Slave" and "servant" follow the project's usual rule for this word.

decisions.choice: "Bwana wangu" with a capital only because it begins the question; "mtumwa" (L), "mtumishi" (B, R); no deity_pronoun spans for the commander
alternatives: "bwana wangu" in lowercase within a sentence
decisions.reason: Joshua uses the ordinary polite address to a superior. Swahili "bwana" serves both as "sir" and "Lord", so the capital here comes only from its place at the start of Joshua's words; the text does not say whether the commander is the LORD himself, and the Swahili, like the English, gives him no capitalised pronouns.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שַׂר־צְבָ֨א יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ שַׁל־נַֽעַלְךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔ךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֑וּא וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ כֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] commander of [the] army of YHWH to Joshua, take off your sandal from on your foot, for the place that you [are] standing on it, holy [is] it. And did Joshua so.

en.L: And the commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you [are] standing, it [is] holy." And Joshua did so.
en.B: The commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Take the sandals off your feet. The place you are standing on is holy." And Joshua did so.
en.R: The commander of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s army told Joshua, "Take off your sandals. You are standing in a holy place." And Joshua did what he said.

sw.L: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Yoshua, "Vua kiatu chako mguuni mwako, kwa maana mahali hapo unaposimama ni patakatifu." Yoshua akafanya hivyo.
sw.B: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Vua viatu miguuni mwako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama ni patakatifu." Naye Yoshua akafanya hivyo.
sw.R: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Vua viatu vyako. Umesimama mahali patakatifu." Naye Yoshua akafanya kama alivyoambiwa.

decisions.choice: take off your sandal ... the place ... is holy: the words spoken to Moses at the burning bush
decisions.reason: The command is almost the same as Exodus 3:5. As the LORD met Moses before he led Israel out of Egypt, so Joshua is met before he leads Israel into the land (compare 1:5; 3:7). The place is holy because the LORD's presence is there, not because of anything in the ground itself.

decisions.choice: your sandal ... your foot: a singular meant as a whole
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular, where Exodus 3:5 has the plural. The singular stands for both; Joshua is to go barefoot.

decisions.choice: Joshua did so: the scene ends with his obedience
decisions.reason: No further words are reported here. The next verses describe Jericho shut tight (6:1), and the LORD then speaks to Joshua (6:2), so the commander's coming leads into the taking of the city.

decisions.choice: sandals ... feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which is what the singular means here (m2).
